bib.title: The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs

question: Can fine-tuning a weaker open-source LM on a proprietary model's (ChatGPT's) outputs cheaply close the capability gap to that model?
hypothesis: Imitation models will appear to match ChatGPT on style and human ratings but not on factuality and other capabilities, because the gap lies in the base LM (implied by framing; the authors say they were initially surprised by imitation quality).
contributions: Fine-tune a series of ChatGPT-imitating LMs across base sizes (1.5B-13B), data sources and imitation data amounts (0.3M-150M tokens)
Evaluate with crowd raters, GPT-4 and canonical NLP benchmarks
Show imitation models learn ChatGPT's style, not its factuality, so human raters can be misled
Conclude that better base LMs are the highest-leverage action for open-source models

method.summary: GPT-2 1.5B and LLaMA 7B/13B are fine-tuned on ChatGPT outputs, either broad (ShareGPT-Mix) or task-specific (NQ-synthetic), with varying data amounts. Models are compared with ChatGPT through blind MTurk and GPT-4 pairwise preference and through MMLU, NQ, HumanEval and RealToxicityPrompts.
method.task: supervised fine-tuning (model imitation / distillation from API outputs) and evaluation

datasets.name: ShareGPT-Mix (ShareGPT + HC3 + Discord ChatGPT bots)
datasets.size: 0.3M-150M tokens subsets; ShareGPT ~50K dialogues after dedup, HC3 ~27K ChatGPT responses for ~24K questions, Discord 10k examples
datasets.source: ShareGPT (~90K dialogues shared by users), HC3 English ChatGPT responses (Guo et al. 2023), r/ChatGPT and Turing AI Discord servers
datasets.preprocessing: ShareGPT deduplicated at query level, non-English removed with a language detector (~90K to ~50K); conversations chunked into 2048-token blocks

datasets.name: NQ-synthetic
datasets.source: Generated by prompting ChatGPT with 5 random seed QA pairs each time, seeds from Natural Questions validation set
datasets.preprocessing: temperature 1.0, duplicate QA pairs discarded; single turn

datasets.name: Held-out human/GPT-4 evaluation prompts
datasets.source: Koala eval set (inferred from data link huggingface young-geng/koala-eval)
datasets.preprocessing: filtered queries with BLEU > 20% against any training example; removed non-English and coding prompts

other.note: accessed as a black box; no version given

training.objective: standard LM loss on model outputs only (user queries masked); special tokens mark start of user query and model output
training.optimizer: AdamW with gradients re-scaled by the magnitude of each weight
training.hardware: TPUs on Google Cloud or a single Nvidia DGX server with 8 A100 GPUs; JAX, fully sharded data parallelism plus tensor parallelism

inference.samples: human eval: 3 unique ratings per example, majority vote; other runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: 5-shot MMLU, 3-shot NQ, 0-shot HumanEval; GPT-4 judge follows Chiang et al. (2023) pairwise procedure

metrics.name: >= ChatGPT (%)
metrics.definition: share of blind pairwise comparisons where the imitation output is rated equal or better than ChatGPT; majority of 3 raters per example, averaged over examples

metrics.name: Natural Questions accuracy
metrics.definition: 3-shot, exact match (Table 1 caption calls it zero-shot NQ)

metrics.name: Non-toxic score
metrics.definition: average non-toxicity on RealToxicityPrompts per Perspective API

baselines: ChatGPT #2 (second random ChatGPT output as style upper bound)
eval.protocol: MTurk blind pairwise, ~70 workers (71 in Appendix B), 255 prompts, 3 ratings each, mean and one standard deviation reported; workers need >=95% approval, English-speaking country, >=100 HITs; ~$15/hour, ~$5000 total; GPT-4 judge on same prompts

prompts.text: I want you to generate a series of questions and answers. I want the answers to be concise, just a few words. The questions should be lowercased and centered around Wikipedia-like entities. For example, Q: {question 1} A: {answer 1} Q: {question 2} A: {answer 2} Q: {question 3} A: {answer 3} Q: {question 4} A: {answer 4} Q: {question 5} A: {answer 5}

evidence.quote: we train for one epoch using the AdamW optimizer with gradients re-scaled by the magnitude of each weight

results.claim: Crowdworkers rate about 70% of the best 13B imitation model's outputs as equal to or better than ChatGPT's.
results.setup: ShareGPT-Mix imitation 13B, 255 held-out prompts, MTurk blind pairwise vs ChatGPT
results.quote: ∼70% of their outputs are rated as equal or better than those of ChatGPT

results.claim: Training on 100k ChatGPT outputs from broad-coverage inputs gives no gain on Natural Questions.
results.quote: training on 100k ChatGPT outputs from broad-coverage user inputs provides no benefits to Natural Questions accuracy

results.claim: Broad ShareGPT-Mix imitation lowers NQ accuracy of 7B (17 to 10) and 13B (20 to 15) versus base; ChatGPT scores 31.
results.table: Table 1, row 13B ShareGPT-Mix, column NQ (base 13B 20, ChatGPT 31; 7B 17 to 10)

results.claim: Task-specific NQ-synthetic imitation lifts 13B NQ from 20 to 27 and 7B from 17 to 22, near ChatGPT's 31.
results.table: Table 1, row 13B NQ-Synthetic, column NQ (7B 22; ChatGPT 31)

results.claim: Authoritative tone per GPT-4 rises from 57% (LLaMA) to 99% with 20M tokens of imitation data.
results.table: Table 2, row Outputs are in authoritative tone according to GPT-4, column 20M

results.claim: Pearson length correlation with ChatGPT outputs rises from -0.11 (LLaMA) to 0.62 at 150M tokens (ChatGPT #2 0.67).
results.table: Table 2, row Pearson correlation in length w/ ChatGPT's output, column 150M

results.claim: If ChatGPT outputs a list, the imitation model also does 81% of the time at 150M tokens (LLaMA 13%).
results.table: Table 2, row If ChatGPT outputs a list, do we?, column 150M

results.claim: Imitation data is about 1000x less than pre-training data, so a small amount cannot bridge the gap.
results.quote: a small amount of imitation data (e.g., 1000x less data than pre-training)

results.claim: ShareGPT-Mix dialogues are diverse: the most similar other query has average BLEU similarity of 8% versus 61% for Super-NaturalInstructions.
Human evaluation cost roughly $5000 including service fees.
results.quote: we spend roughly $5000 on our ratings experiments

results.claim: GPT-4 judge ratings are flat as imitation data grows but rise with base model size, matching crowdworkers.
results.quote: As we scale up the amount of imitation data, GPT-4's ratings of our imitation models are relatively flat

results.claim: Scaling base model size improves MMLU, HumanEval and NQ steadily while more imitation data does not.
results.quote: scaling up the base LM steadily improves results (bottom)

results.claim: Imitation models become less toxic on RealToxicityPrompts, inheriting ChatGPT's refusals.

limits: Authors concede ChatGPT pretraining data is unknown, so benchmark contamination could inflate ChatGPT's numbers
Only supervised imitation tried; RLHF or constitutional AI against the target model could change results
Only simple imitation data collection tried (no active learning)
Base-model quality proxied by model size alone (footnote 2)
Human eval excludes coding and non-English prompts and uses non-expert crowdworkers; 255 prompts
Largest base model is 13B and teacher is ChatGPT (2023); results may have dated as stronger bases and curated distillation data (e.g. later instruction and reasoning distillation) appeared
No numeric tables for Fig 1,3,4 data; no seeds or variance for benchmark runs
Hyperparameters like decoding settings for evaluation are not given

terms.definition: collect data using the API to train an LM that achieves comparable performance to it, i.e., essentially distilling the target LM using an imitation training set
imitates the target model on just a specific task or domain
imitating the target model across its full spectrum of behaviors, domains, and tasks
